notes.query_counting: Query count tracked via custom DBAL Middleware (QueryCountingMiddleware) that intercepts prepare(), query() and exec() calls.
notes.join_fetch: Doctrine 3.6.7 DQL parser fails to parse JOIN FETCH syntax ('Class FETCH is not defined'). A4 and B1 use native SQL with ResultSetMappingBuilder as a workaround. This is a known Doctrine 3.x issue. See: https://github.com/doctrine/orm/issues
notes.proxy_classes: isDevMode: true is used to auto-generate proxy classes on each run. Production mode (false) requires pre-generated proxies which are lost between Docker container restarts. This adds minor overhead to the first iteration only (warm-up phase).
notes.A4: Native SQL with ResultSetMappingBuilder — single JOIN query. n_warmup: 2000 because random order_id causes high CV; warm-up did not converge within limit.
notes.B1: Native SQL with ResultSetMappingBuilder — single JOIN across 4 tables. n_warmup: 2000 for same reason as A4.
notes.B3: query_count_median: 2 — Doctrine counts both the main query and a secondary query for the tags JOIN.
notes.C2: Uses DBAL connection directly (em->getConnection()) — query_count: 2 (UPDATE delivered + UPDATE shipped). See methodology/c2_limit_analysis.json.
notes.D1: query_count_median: 21 — Doctrine Unit of Work batches all INSERTs in a single flush (1 SELECT user + 1 INSERT order + 5 INSERT items + 1 UPDATE total + 13 sequence queries for ID generation).

A1.description: Simple SELECT by primary key via EntityManager::find()

A2.description: Filtered list with ORDER BY and LIMIT via DQL

A3.description: N+1 diagnostic — 100 orders, lazy-loads user per order via proxy (intentional)

A4.description: Eager loading via native SQL JOIN — single query (JOIN FETCH workaround, see notes)

B1.description: Deep eager load via native SQL JOIN across 4 tables — single query (JOIN FETCH workaround, see notes)

B2.description: Aggregate with GROUP BY via DQL — categories with product count and avg price

B3.description: Many-to-many via DQL — products by tag with category JOIN FETCH

C1.description: Bulk insert — 10,000 products in chunks of 500 via DBAL executeStatement()

C2.description: Bulk update — UPDATE FROM subquery, LIMIT 1000 rows via DBAL (see methodology/c2_limit_analysis.json)

D1.description: Unit of Work — persist order + 5 items, single flush, 21 queries (includes sequence queries for ID generation)
